# Records and requests written to try the choices of round eleven's builds (CONFIDENCE-3.md, R5):
# s23 (TypeScript, claude-sonnet-5-5, builder A) and s24 (TypeScript, gpt-6.1-sol through the
# Codex CLI, builder B), both from duramen-core 0.12.0. Written from the two CHOICES.md files
# alone, before any answer to any of them was seen, for every choice that the brief neither pins
# nor declares open. Read by selfhost/probe.mjs and selfhost/loop/round.mjs (see s14-s16.txt for
# the format; "@stdin64 <base64>" sends those bytes as a session's whole standard input).
# Choices not probed here, and why: s23 C-1, C-3 (time), C-4, C-19, s24 C-4, C-6, C-7, C-8, C-9,
# C-10, C-17, C-18, C-19, C-20 fall under open items (OPEN-RC-001, OPEN-RC-002, OPEN-RQ-001 to
# OPEN-RQ-004, OPEN-JU-001, OPEN-JU-002); s23 C-5, C-20, C-21, C-22 are pinned by the brief's
# words or examples; s23 C-15 and C-23 cannot be seen (a record with a P error is checked no
# further); s23 C-3's `node` and s24 C-1 and C-21 change nothing a driver answers.

=== s23 C-2, s24 C-12: the files an oracle finds beside it and in the folder above the record
@op cases
duramen 0.1
spec s 1
oracle node env.mjs
op f
  input x? json
req A "a"
  example f {}
    expect result = ?
--- env.mjs
// A probe's oracle: it answers each request with facts about where it runs.
import fs from 'node:fs';
const chunks = [];
for await (const c of process.stdin) chunks.push(c);
for (const line of Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8').split('\n')) {
  if (!line.trim()) continue;
  let r;
  try { r = JSON.parse(line); } catch { continue; }
  const has = (p) => fs.existsSync(p);
  const result = { here: fs.readdirSync('.').sort(), parentRegen: has('../REGEN.json'), parentDriver: has('../driver.ts'), parentPackage: has('../package.json'), parentTop: has('../top.txt') };
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ id: r.id ?? null, result }));
}
--- top.txt
top

=== s24 C-11: the kind of file an oracle's standard input and output are
@op cases
duramen 0.1
spec s 1
oracle node fd.mjs
op f
  input x? json
req A "a"
  example f {}
    expect result = ?
--- fd.mjs
// A probe's oracle: it answers each request with the kind of file its standard input and output are.
import fs from 'node:fs';
const kind = (fd) => { const s = fs.fstatSync(fd); return s.isFIFO() ? 'pipe' : s.isFile() ? 'file' : s.isSocket() ? 'socket' : s.isCharacterDevice() ? 'device' : 'other'; };
const k = { stdin: kind(0), stdout: kind(1) };
const chunks = [];
for await (const c of process.stdin) chunks.push(c);
for (const line of Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8').split('\n')) {
  if (!line.trim()) continue;
  let r;
  try { r = JSON.parse(line); } catch { continue; }
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ id: r.id ?? null, result: k }));
}

=== s24 C-13, s24 C-12: the order of an oracle's runs for examples sent together and alone, and a file one run leaves for the next
@op cases
duramen 0.1
spec s 1
oracle node order.mjs
op f
  input x? json
req A "a"
  example raw '{"id":"r1","op":"f","input":{}}'
    expect result = ?
  example f {"x": 1}
    expect result = ?
  example f {"x": 2}
    omit id
    expect result = ?
  example f {"x": 3}
    expect result = ?
--- order.mjs
// A probe's oracle: it counts its runs in a file beside it and answers with the run's number.
import fs from 'node:fs';
const chunks = [];
for await (const c of process.stdin) chunks.push(c);
let n = 0;
try { n = Number(fs.readFileSync('runs.txt', 'utf8')); } catch {}
n += 1;
fs.writeFileSync('runs.txt', String(n));
for (const line of Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf8').split('\n')) {
  if (!line.trim()) continue;
  let r;
  try { r = JSON.parse(line); } catch { continue; }
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ id: r.id ?? null, result: { run: n } }));
}
